rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at moderate temperature to elute all 10 compounds if possible and reveal the overall elution window without risking truncation. This gives a first read on whether peaks are compressed early, spread across the gradient, or still retained into the hold.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only way to improve CRF is to shorten the run while keeping every pair above 1.5. The first run suggests the full 0.05-0.95 window is wider than needed, so trim the high end and steepen modestly to pull the last peak earlier without making the gradient excessively abrupt.

We are very close to ideal, with only pair 6/7 slightly below 1.5 after compressing the method. Keep the successful phi window and temperature, then lengthen the gradient one step to recover that marginal resolution while aiming to keep the last peak at or just under 10 minutes.

Pair 6/7 appears only weakly sensitive to slope, so temperature is the cleaner lever to try for a small selectivity change while also shaving the last peak below 10 minutes. Keep the near-optimal 12 min, 0.05-0.75 window and raise T one step to test whether the critical pair reorders or separates slightly without losing overall speed.

The critical pair is highly temperature-sensitive, so revert to 40 C. To keep the run fast while nudging the 6/7 pair back above 1.5, widen the gradient window slightly at the high end, which should reduce compression of the mid-late cluster without the large time penalty seen from lengthening tG.

At 0.05-0.80, 12 min gets the last peak under 10 min but still leaves the 6/7 pair short of 1.5, so the next best move is a one-step shallower gradient in the same window. This should tell us whether that pair can cross 1.5 with only a small time penalty, potentially improving on the current best CRF.

The key pair responds strongly to temperature, so lower T one step from the successful fast method to try to gain selectivity on 6/7 while preserving the sub-10-minute last peak. This is a targeted test of whether cooler conditions can push that pair above 1.5 without the time penalty of a longer gradient.

Temperature changes hurt selectivity, so stay at 40 C and explore the phi window instead. Narrowing the high end from 0.75 to 0.70 should slightly shallow the gradient around the mid-eluting cluster where the critical pair sits, while likely keeping the last peak close enough to 10 minutes to challenge the current best.

The first peak is still comfortably retained, so raising phi0 should trim dead time and may shorten the run without strongly disturbing the late cluster. This tests whether we can keep the favorable sub-10-minute last peak of the 0.80 window while improving the marginal mid-pair resolution enough to beat the current best.

Injection 9 improved the time term to zero, so now the best chance is to recover a little resolution on the 6/7 pair without pushing the last peak past 10 minutes. Lowering phi1 one step should slightly shallow the gradient around the critical mid-late cluster while keeping the run compact because phi0 is already raised.

We have reached the maximum CRF, so this is now a boundary-mapping run to see whether an even shorter practical method exists on the plateau. Raising phi0 one step should reduce retention further; if full resolution is maintained with t_last still under 10 minutes, it confirms a faster equivalent optimum, and if not we already know injection 10 is ideal.

Injection 11 kept full resolution while shortening the run further, so continue pushing phi0 upward to find the fastest method on the CRF=1.000 plateau. This directly probes how close the first peak can approach the dead-time region before the critical 6/7 pair or early retention starts to fail.

Since 0.20 at the low end over-compressed the critical 6/7 pair, step back to the successful phi0 0.15 and now trim phi1 one step to see whether the upper window can be narrowed while preserving CRF 1.000. This is a plateau-refinement test for an even tighter fully resolved method with the same fast runtime.

With phi0 0.15 established as the fastest low-end setting that still fully resolves the critical pair, test one step higher phi1 to see if the broader upper window can pull the last peak even earlier while staying on the CRF=1.000 plateau. This maps the other side of the optimum around the successful 0.15-0.75, 12 min condition.

We have defined a CRF=1.000 plateau at 12 min, so the highest-value remaining test is whether the same selective window can be shortened one step in gradient time and still hold all pairs at or above 1.5. If it fails, injections 10 and 11 remain optimal; if it succeeds, it would reveal a faster equivalent optimum.

The 10 min test confirms the critical pair is the limiting factor for further slope compression, so probe whether a temperature change can preserve full resolution in the proven 12 min window while cutting runtime further. This checks if any faster CRF=1.000 plateau exists at a different temperature, even though 45 C was unfavorable at lower phi0.

High temperature clearly collapses the critical pair, so check the opposite direction at the proven 0.15-0.75, 12 min window. If 35 C preserves full resolution while keeping t_last under 10 min, it would match the maximum CRF and further define the robustness of the optimum; otherwise 40 C is confirmed as the unique sweet spot.

The 12 min methods define the optimum, but a 14 min run at phi0 0.10 can quantify how much robustness margin exists on the critical 6/7 pair around the best condition. This is a useful confirmatory point near the optimum since injection 2 was borderline and injection 10 reached full score.

The remaining unexplored neighbor of the best method is a slightly lower phi1 at the same phi0, tG, and temperature. This tests whether the 0.10 low end combined with a narrower upper window can still keep t_last under 10 minutes while increasing the critical 6/7 resolution margin relative to the best run.

Since the local method space around the optimum is mostly mapped at 40 C, test the best geometric settings at 45 C to verify whether temperature ever improves speed without sacrificing the critical 6/7 pair. This is the most direct thermal robustness check against the current champion.

Complete the temperature bracket at the best geometric settings to confirm whether 40 C is truly the only temperature that keeps all pairs above 1.5. This final nearby check resolves whether cooling helps or shifts the critical overlap to the neighboring pair, as seen in other runs.

With the local optimum established, use a remaining injection to confirm robustness on the slower side for the equally scoring phi0 0.15 condition. This should show how much extra resolution margin exists for the critical pair at only modest additional runtime and helps validate 0.15-0.75, 12 min, 40 C as a stable operating point.

Use a remaining injection to map the faster side beyond phi1 0.80 while keeping the proven phi0 0.10 and temperature. This tests whether a slightly wider upper window can further reduce t_last yet perhaps still maintain enough selectivity on the critical 6/7 pair, sharpening the boundary around the optimum.

One remaining boundary test is to combine the faster successful low end, phi0 0.15, with a higher phi1 to see whether the upper window can be expanded before the critical pair drops below 1.5. This finishes mapping the fast side around the two CRF=1.000 methods.

For the final injection, test the remaining compact window adjacent to the mapped optimum to complete the boundary on both ends of phi. This checks whether simultaneously raising phi0 and lowering phi1 can keep the critical pair resolved while producing the shortest sub-10-minute method, although current data suggest the 6/7 pair is likely the limiting constraint.
